hunks.baseline: Unlike modern prisons, where the concept of human rights has been mixed in just enough to make them palatable, the underground prisons found throughout the Murim served their purpose exceptionally well.
hunks.sol: Unlike modern prisons, where human rights have been mixed in just enough to make them palatable, underground prisons in the Murim served their purpose exceptionally well.

hunks.baseline: The word *human rights* did not exist here in the first place.
hunks.sol: The concept of human rights didn’t exist here in the first place.

hunks.baseline: The underground prison of the Sichuan Tang Clan, for example, had been closer to a torture chamber than a place meant merely to lock up criminals.
hunks.sol: The underground prison of the Sichuan Tang Clan, for example, had been closer to a torture chamber than a place meant to hold prisoners.

hunks.baseline: Even the old guard who had died during Dark Heaven’s attack had been a torture expert with several decades of experience. He would often reminisce about his prime with a pleased smile.
hunks.sol: Even the old guard who had died during Dark Heaven’s attack had been a torture expert with decades of experience. He would often reminisce about his prime with a pleased smile.

hunks.baseline: “Those days right after the Great Faction War were wonderful. We caught three or four notorious fiends every day—counting them like animals, of course.”
hunks.sol: “Those days right after the Great Faction War were wonderful. We had three or four head of notorious fiends brought in every day.”

hunks.baseline: “…Like animals? Not people?”
hunks.sol: “…Head? Not people?”

hunks.baseline: “Yes. When we lined up fifteen or so of the beasts and got to work, the response was incredible. They were so happy they nearly passed out.”
hunks.sol: “Yes. Line up a dozen or so and get to work, and the response was incredible. They’d scream themselves silly with delight.”

hunks.baseline: He even counted people the way one counted animals.
hunks.sol: He even counted people the way you counted animals.

hunks.baseline: I had never bothered to ask for details about what had happened back then, but it was difficult to imagine prisoners nearly passing out from happiness just because he had given them pretty tattoos with the small knife he kept so carefully tucked into his belt.
hunks.sol: I had never bothered to ask for details, but it was hard to imagine prisoners screaming with delight because he’d given them pretty irezumi tattoos with the small knife he kept tucked so carefully into his belt.

hunks.baseline: I had gone a little off track, but in any case, most underground prisons in the Murim were more or less the same, with only minor differences.
hunks.sol: I’d gone a little off track. Anyway, most underground prisons in the Murim were more or less the same.

hunks.baseline: Just like the underground prison of the Nanman Beast Palace where I was currently locked up. And…
hunks.sol: Just like the underground prison of the Nanman Beast Palace where I was locked up. And…

hunks.baseline: “Pavilion Master. Taishan hungry. Got locked in underground prison because Taishan eats too much.”
hunks.sol: “Taishan. Hungry. Got locked in underground prison because they said Taishan eats too much.”

hunks.baseline: In a way, it was the result of an old, poorly built prison and a considerable impact coming together in one incredible coincidence.
hunks.sol: In a way, it was a coincidence born of an aging, poorly built prison taking a considerable blow.

hunks.baseline: I stared blankly at the ceiling. Then I gave a quiet laugh toward Taishan, who was blinking his enormous eyes through the small hole above me.
hunks.sol: I stared blankly at the ceiling, then gave a quiet laugh at Taishan, who was blinking his enormous eyes through the small hole above me.

hunks.baseline: It might have seemed like a completely pointless conversation, but every time I saw his eyes peering through the gap, I couldn’t stop a laugh from escaping.
hunks.sol: It was a conversation that made no sense out of context, but every time I saw his eyes peering through the gap, I couldn’t help laughing.

hunks.baseline: Meeting a familiar face was one thing. More importantly, I might be able to get out of here sooner than expected.
hunks.sol: Seeing a familiar face was one thing. If things went well, I might be able to get out of here sooner than expected.

hunks.baseline: Of course, there was also the fact that he was the only person who could answer the question that concerned me most.
hunks.sol: Besides, Taishan was the only person who could answer the question worrying me most.

hunks.baseline: At my question, his enormous calf-like eyes grew damp.
hunks.sol: At my question, his enormous calf-like eyes filled with tears.

hunks.baseline: A sense of foreboding rushed over me. I hurriedly opened my mouth.
“Don’t just bawl. Tell me properly. What happened?”
hunks.sol: Dread hit me. I hurried to ask, “Stop sniveling and tell me what happened.”

hunks.baseline: “Taishan… sniff. It couldn’t be helped. It’s so unfair.”
hunks.sol: “Taishan… sniff. Couldn’t help it. It’s so unfair.”

hunks.baseline: Damn it. My vision went dark. I could already see the members of the Fire Dragon Pavilion lying before me as cold corpses.
hunks.sol: Damn it. My vision went dark. I could already picture the members of the Fire Dragon Pavilion lying there as cold corpses.

hunks.baseline: *Or torture? But how could they do that?*
hunks.sol: *Or were they tortured? But how could they do that?*

hunks.baseline: It had only been half a day since I surrendered on the condition that the Fire Dragon Pavilion members would be kept safe.
hunks.sol: It had only been half a day since I’d surrendered on the condition that the Fire Dragon Pavilion members would be kept safe.

hunks.baseline: This was something the Beast Miao King himself had promised. No matter how powerful Baeksang’s faction had become, this was impossible.
hunks.sol: The Beast Miao King himself had promised me. No matter how powerful Baeksang’s faction had become, they couldn’t do this.

hunks.baseline: Just as I was muttering those words hollowly inside my head, Taishan spoke in a damp voice.
hunks.sol: Just as the thought ran hollowly through my head, Taishan spoke through his tears.

hunks.baseline: “I hate Lord too. I hate Namho too. Taishan is so unfairly treated.”
hunks.sol: “Taishan hates Lord. Hates Namho too. It’s so unfair.”

hunks.baseline: “Pavilion Master. In that case, do you have anything to eat?”
hunks.sol: “Pavilion Master. Speaking of which, do you have anything to eat?”

hunks.baseline: After remaining silent for a moment, I answered with all the sincerity in my heart.
hunks.sol: I fell silent for a moment, then answered from the bottom of my heart.

hunks.baseline: As my blood pressure soared, rage took control of my entire body. Since being locked in the underground prison, I had never thrashed around so violently in anger.
hunks.sol: My blood pressure shot up, and rage took over my entire body. I thrashed harder than I had at any point since being locked in the underground prison.

hunks.baseline: If not for these goddamn heavy iron balls, I would have started by punching that bastard in the mouth.
hunks.sol: If not for these goddamn heavy iron balls, I would’ve started by punching that bastard in the face.

hunks.baseline: “Namho and Lord are safe. They are being held in different places, so Taishan doesn’t know much, but the White Tiger’s master told Taishan.”
hunks.sol: “Namho and Lord are doing well. They’re being held in different places, so Taishan doesn’t know much, but White Tiger’s master told Taishan.”

hunks.baseline: “The White Tiger’s master? Yayul Mok?”
hunks.sol: “White Tiger’s master? Yayul Mok?”

hunks.baseline: It seemed the Beast Miao King had made arrangements after all. I stopped thrashing around in anger and let out a sigh of relief.
hunks.sol: It seemed the Beast Miao King had stepped in after all. I stopped thrashing and let out a sigh of relief.

hunks.baseline: “Taishan has been hungry for two shichen already. Taishan’s mind is hazy.”
hunks.sol: “Taishan hasn’t eaten for two whole shichen. Taishan’s mind is hazy.”

hunks.baseline: “…People don’t usually call it hunger after two shichen. More importantly, how did you end up locked in here? Great Hero Yayul would’ve stopped it before it got this far. There’s no way you were locked up just for eating too much.”
hunks.sol: “…Most people wouldn’t call two shichen without food starving. Anyway, how did you end up locked in here? Great Hero Yayul would’ve stopped them if it was anything minor. There’s no way they locked you up just for eating too much.”

hunks.baseline: “Taishan was treated unfairly. A Nanman man was going to leave after giving Taishan food the size of mouse droppings, so Taishan grabbed his wrist and asked for more. His bone broke.”
hunks.sol: “Taishan was treated unfairly. A Nanman man was going to leave after giving Taishan a mouse-dropping-sized portion of food. Taishan grabbed his wrist to ask for more, and the bone broke.”

hunks.baseline: “Taishan was surprised and grabbed his other wrist. That one broke too. This was obviously a trap.”
hunks.sol: “Taishan was surprised and grabbed his other wrist. That one broke too. It was obviously a trap.”

hunks.baseline: “…Come down. This time, really come down.”
hunks.sol: “…Come down. This time, I mean it.”

hunks.baseline: I was already struggling to keep a low profile, and this bastard had broken both arms of the man who came to feed him?
hunks.sol: We needed to keep our heads down, and this bastard had broken both wrists of the man who came to feed him?

hunks.baseline: *I entered the tiger’s den to save a bastard like that?*
hunks.sol: *I walked into the tiger’s den to save a bastard like that?*

hunks.baseline: After barely calming my fury, I asked,
“Then what about the others? Not Namho or Sama Pyo. Everyone else?”
hunks.sol: Once I’d barely managed to calm down, I asked, “What about the others? Besides Namho and Sama Pyo.”

hunks.baseline: “Yes. But they said they weren’t coming here. Taishan doesn’t know why, but the White Tiger’s master said it was safer that way.”
hunks.sol: “Yeah. But they said they weren’t coming here. Taishan doesn’t know why, but White Tiger’s master said it was safer that way.”

hunks.baseline: Hearing that even the three members of the reconnaissance squad had been captured made my heart feel heavy for a moment. But I agreed with Yayul Mok that they would be much safer there.
hunks.sol: For a moment, my heart sank at the news that all three had been captured. But I agreed with Yayul Mok: they were safer with the reconnaissance squad.

hunks.baseline: *Baeksang’s influence can’t reach that place for now.*
hunks.sol: *Baeksang’s influence can’t reach that far right now.*

hunks.baseline: The two tribal chieftains leading the reconnaissance squad were loyal to the Beast Miao King.

hunks.baseline: What was more, some of the Nanman people I had rescued from the Poisonblood Grounds were their kinsmen. Unlike the other chieftains who had turned to Baeksang’s side, they wouldn’t easily switch allegiances.
hunks.sol: The two tribal chieftains leading the squad were loyal to the Beast Miao King. Some of the Nanman people I’d rescued from the Poisonblood Grounds were their kinsmen, too. Unlike the other chieftains who had gone over to Baeksang, they wouldn’t switch sides easily.

hunks.baseline: *The three of them are more likely to be in danger than they are now if the reconnaissance squad runs into the Blood Monk.*
hunks.sol: *The real danger will come if the reconnaissance squad runs into the Blood Monk.*

hunks.baseline: The Blood Monk was an unidentified old monster who had stained Guizhou with blood all by himself, wielding Supreme Peak martial prowess.
hunks.sol: The Blood Monk was an unidentified old monster who had stained Guizhou with blood single-handedly, wielding Supreme Peak martial prowess.

hunks.baseline: Almost nothing was known about him. But if he really was a subordinate of the Southern Heaven Demon Empress, as I suspected, then the situation would become the worst it could possibly be.
hunks.sol: Almost nothing was known about him. But if he really was a subordinate of the Southern Heaven Demon Empress, as I suspected, things could take the worst possible turn.

hunks.baseline: He would certainly head south on the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s orders. And if he encountered the reconnaissance squad, the three people among them would fall into his hands as well.
hunks.sol: He would be heading south on her orders. If he met the reconnaissance squad, the three of them would fall into his hands as well.

hunks.sol: But right now, I couldn’t do anything about them.

hunks.baseline: They were still on the move at that very moment, while I was trapped in a prison deep underground, unable to move an inch.
hunks.sol: They were on the move even now, while I was trapped deep underground, unable to move an inch.

hunks.baseline: *All I can do is hope my guess about the Blood Monk is wrong.*
hunks.sol: *All I can do is hope I’m wrong about the Blood Monk.*

hunks.baseline: So there were only two things I could do right now.
hunks.sol: So there were only two things I could do.

hunks.baseline: The first was prayer.
hunks.sol: The first was pray.

*I have no idea who developed the System, but they came up with one hell of a shitty Quest title.*

hunks.baseline: Among the countless martial artists in the continent, river pirates were an especially rough and free-spirited bunch.
hunks.sol: Among the countless martial artists on the continent, river pirates were an especially rough and free-spirited bunch.

hunks.baseline: They didn’t want to be oppressed by various laws, didn’t want to be arrested by the authorities, and didn’t particularly want to live decent lives, either.
hunks.sol: They didn’t want laws restricting them or the authorities arresting them. They didn’t want to live decent lives, either.

hunks.baseline: Unlike his father, who had ended his life as a good fisherman, Sudal had boldly resolved to live and die as a man of adventure.
hunks.sol: Unlike his father, who had lived and died a good fisherman, Sudal had boldly resolved to live and die as an adventurer.

hunks.baseline: He had lived the life of a fairly successful river pirate.
But lately, he had begun to feel increasingly doubtful about what he was doing.
hunks.sol: He’d done fairly well as a river pirate. Only recently had he begun to wonder what he was doing with his life.

hunks.baseline: He wasn’t doing anything.
Every day, he sat at the bow and stared at the calm river. When the sunlight became too hot, he went swimming.
hunks.sol: Nothing. Every day, he sat at the bow and stared at the calm river. When the sun got too hot, he went swimming. That was all.

hunks.baseline: That was all.

His immediate superior, who lorded over the Yangtze in Sichuan, had been summoned to League headquarters by the venerable Alliance Leader. Meanwhile, Sudal and his men had drifted down the tributaries all the way to the backwater of Yunnan, wasting their time.
hunks.sol: His immediate superior, who ruled the Yangtze in Sichuan, had been summoned to League headquarters by the revered Alliance Leader. Meanwhile, Sudal and his men had come down the tributaries to backwater Yunnan and were wasting their days.

hunks.sol: *By now, merchant ships loaded with valuables must be passing through Sichuan.*

hunks.baseline: Sudal knew that and desperately wanted to return immediately. But every time he did, one man’s presence kept flashing before his eyes.
hunks.sol: Sudal desperately wanted to go back. But every time he thought about it, one man’s face appeared before him.

hunks.baseline: That was the boast he had made seven days and nights ago.
hunks.sol: That was the boast he’d made seven days and nights ago. Naturally, he hadn’t meant a word of it.

hunks.baseline: Naturally, it had been empty words without even a single ounce of sincerity behind them.
But the much younger man had merely smiled warmly and answered,
hunks.sol: But the much younger man had smiled warmly and answered,

hunks.baseline: “Heh heh. Did someone stick a marlin in your ear? I said stay here. I’ll need to ask you for another favor when we head back, too.”
hunks.sol: “Heh heh. Did someone stick a marlin in your ear? I said stay nearby. I’ll need another favor when we head back.”

hunks.baseline: “Great Hero Jin, forgive me, but we have a livelihood to maintain…”
hunks.sol: “Great Hero Jin, forgive me, but we have a living to make…”

hunks.baseline: “A livelihood. That’s nice. But you need to be alive to make a living, don’t you?”
hunks.sol: “A living. That’s nice. But you have to be alive to make one, don’t you?”

hunks.baseline: It was called a favor, but in reality, it was a threat.
hunks.sol: He called it a favor, but it was a threat.

hunks.baseline: But what could Sudal do? In the Murim, the one with stronger martial arts was king.
hunks.sol: What could Sudal do? In the Murim, whoever had the stronger martial arts was king.

hunks.baseline: And to make matters worse, that monstrous young man’s Master was a crazy old monster who was actually called a king.
hunks.sol: Worse, that monstrous young man’s Master was a crazy old monster who really was called a king.

hunks.baseline: Swallowing his tears, Sudal had nodded. In the end, he had spent more than seven days and nights catching fish in a tributary at the edge of Yunnan where not even a small boat could be seen.
hunks.sol: Swallowing his tears, Sudal had nodded. For more than seven days and nights, he and his men had stayed on a tributary at the edge of Yunnan where they couldn’t even spot a small boat, doing nothing but catching fish.

hunks.baseline: That was how things had been until an idea occurred to him just yesterday.
hunks.sol: Until an idea occurred to him yesterday.

hunks.baseline: *Wait a minute. Do I really need to do this? There’s still plenty of time before that Jin Taekyung bastard comes back.*
hunks.sol: *Wait. Why am I doing this? It’ll be a while before that Jin Taekyung bastard comes back.*

hunks.baseline: Although he had only operated along the Yangtze, Sudal knew what a godforsaken dump Nanman was.
hunks.sol: Sudal had only ever operated on the Yangtze, but even he knew what a godforsaken dump Nanman was.

hunks.baseline: He didn’t know exactly what Jin Taekyung’s mission was, but considering that he had come all the way here, it could not possibly be simple.
hunks.sol: He didn’t know exactly what Jin Taekyung’s mission was. Still, if it had brought him all the way here, it couldn’t be simple.

hunks.baseline: But did he really need to worry about someone who wasn’t even here and whine like a dog that needed to shit?
hunks.sol: So why was Sudal worrying himself sick over a man who wasn’t even around?

hunks.baseline: Sudal seriously reflected on the adventurous life he had lived. Then he gave his men an order.
hunks.sol: He gave his adventurous life some serious thought, then ordered his men,

hunks.sol: “Fuck. If you want to die, die alone. Why should the rest of us get cremated when you’re not even the Stronghold Lord?”

hunks.sol: But Sudal had a plan for that, too.

hunks.baseline: “Dunk that bastard. In the Yangtze. The Yangtze…”
hunks.sol: “Dunk that bastard. The Yangtze… the Yangtze…”

hunks.sol: After two men had gone into the water in quick succession, the complaints stopped. Under Sudal’s spirited command, three swift ships took the western tributary toward Guizhou.

hunks.baseline: At last, after all this time, they found a target.
hunks.sol: At last, they spotted their first target in ages.

hunks.baseline: Just like now.
How long had it been since their last raid?
Sudal stood tall at the stern like a Great General, smiling with satisfaction as the ship drew rapidly closer.
hunks.sol: How long had it been since their last raid? Sudal stood tall at the stern like a Great General, smiling with satisfaction as the ship drew rapidly closer.

hunks.baseline: Then, before fifteen minutes had even passed, he realized that something was wrong.
hunks.sol: Then, before fifteen minutes had passed, he realized something was wrong.

hunks.baseline: The ship had drawn so close that it was almost right in front of them. There was no crew. No captain.
hunks.sol: The ship was almost upon them now. There was no crew and no captain.

hunks.baseline: Only one person was waiting for them.
hunks.sol: Only one person waited for them.

hunks.baseline: “A swift ship of the Yangtze River Channel League. How fortunate.”
hunks.sol: “A swift ship of the Yangtze River Channel League. What fortunate timing.”
